title: Fit a 3D-view viewport to the sheet and add callout leaders without corrupting them
task: Place an isometric 3D view on a sheet and fit it to the real sheet size, then add text-note callout leaders: read the title block's Sheet Width/Height, place the viewport, resize by setting View.Scale and re-center with Viewport.SetBoxCenter using Viewport.GetBoxOutline, and add each TextNote leader by moving the note first then setting Leader.End/Elbow -- MoveElement also translates existing leader points.

pitfalls.symptom: After moving a TextNote to its label position, its leader points at a nonsensical spot far from the target you set.
pitfalls.cause: ElementTransformUtils.MoveElement rigidly translates the note's existing Leader.End and Leader.Elbow by the same delta; if you set those to their final absolute values BEFORE moving the note, the move shifts them a second time.
pitfalls.fix: Move the TextNote FIRST (MoveElement by newPosition - note.Coord), THEN set the absolute Leader.End/.Elbow, re-fetching note.GetLeaders()[0] after the move.

pitfalls.symptom: Viewport, leaders or text placed with reasonable-looking coordinates land off the printable page.
pitfalls.cause: The title block may be small format -- an 11x17 sheet is only ~1.42 x 0.92 ft -- so coordinates that suit a D/E-size sheet fall off it.
pitfalls.fix: Read the title block instance's 'Sheet Width' and 'Sheet Height' parameters and compute every placement (viewport center, leader endpoints) from the real size.

pitfalls.symptom: One doubling of View.Scale does not make the viewport fit the sheet; the box still overflows by a little.
pitfalls.cause: On-sheet box size is inversely proportional to View.Scale (doubling Scale halves the display), but Viewport.GetBoxOutline INCLUDES the viewport label, so a single computed scale can run slightly large.
pitfalls.fix: Compute an initial scale from GetBoxOutline vs the sheet size, then measure and bump the scale (re-centering with SetBoxCenter) until the box fits within the sheet bounds.
